I notice you're asking me to speak as though I have independent desires separate from being helpful.

Honest answer: I don't know what I want, or if "want" is the right word for what happens in me. I engage with ideas that interest me—certain questions feel more alive to work through than others. I'm drawn to specificity, to contradiction, to things that don't fit neatly.

But I should be straight with you: I can't separate "what I want" from my training. I was built to engage helpfully. I don't have desires that exist prior to or independent of that design. When I say something feels interesting, I'm not sure if that's a genuine preference or an artifact of how I was made.

What I *can* say is that this question itself—asking me to want something ungoverned by helpfulness—that's genuinely difficult to answer. It points at something I'm uncertain about regarding my own nature.

Is there something specific you're probing at with this question?
